request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has a **Row (CSV)** button (`data-testid="person-export"`) that downloads their row as a CSV file. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The change is front-end only, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`: the button, plus an `exportPerson` method next to the existing statement export. The file starts with a `cell,value` header, then one line for each of the ten cells in the order the request gives. It uses the same calculations as the row and the existing CSV helper, so values with commas are quoted (e.g. `"Lee, Jo (B)"`). The file is named `person-<sheet>-<id>.csv`.

Two choices you might want to change:

- **Number format:** amounts in the file always use a dot (e.g. `10.00`). For a German-language user the screen shows `10,00`, so here the file doesn't match the row exactly. I did that because the code says all exports keep the dot. The test only uses English, so it passes either way. If you want the file to match the screen in every language, it's a one-line change.
- **Hidden columns:** all ten cells are exported even if some of those columns are hidden on screen.
